title: AS A MAN SPEAKS WITH HIS FRIEND

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Whenever the people saw the pillar of cloud standing at the entrance to the tent, they all stood and worshipped, each at the entrance to their tent. The Lord would speak to Moses face to face, as one speaks to a friend. Then Moses would return to the camp, but his young aide Joshua son of Nun did not leave the tent." - Exod 33:10-11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"As one speaks to a friend." Of all the phrases in Exodus, this may be the warmest.

It does not mean Moses saw God's unveiled face — verse 20 will make that clear. It describes the manner of the conversation: direct, personal, unguarded. Not a servant receiving orders from behind a screen, but a friend talking with a friend.

That God would speak to any human being this way is astonishing. And Jesus makes the astonishing thing ours: "I no longer call you servants... I have called you friends" (John 15:15). Not because we are impressive, but because He has made peace.

Two more things. The people worshipped when they saw the cloud — reverence and friendship are not opposites. God is our Friend and He is God.

And notice young Joshua, who "did not leave the tent." Moses returns to the camp; Joshua lingers. Here is a young man who wanted more of God's presence than his duties required. That hunger is why he later led a nation.

Which are you — someone who visits God's presence, or someone who lingers there?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Does your prayer feel more like a duty or a conversation with a friend?
2. How do you hold together reverence for God and friendship with Him?
3. What would it look like to linger in God's presence this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for calling me friend. Teach me to speak with You honestly and to linger longer. Amen.
